record.context_brief: Existence of normal varieties without Ulrich sheaves
record.original_question: Does there exist a normal projective variety X that admits no Ulrich sheaf?

evidence.quote: Question 4. Does there exist a normal variety X without Ulrich sheaves?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X \subset \mathbb{P}^N$ be a projective variety over an algebraically closed field $k$, embedded by a very ample line bundle $\mathcal{O}_X(1)$. A coherent sheaf $\mathcal{E}$ on $X$ is called an Ulrich sheaf (with respect to $\mathcal{O}_X(1)$) if $\mathcal{E}$ is nonzero and satisfies
$$H^i(X, \mathcal{E}(-j)) = 0 \quad \text{for all } i \geq 0 \text{ and } 1 \leq j \leq \dim X.$$
Equivalently, if $\pi : X \to \mathbb{P}^{\dim X}$ is a finite linear projection, $\mathcal{E}$ is Ulrich if and only if $\pi_* \mathcal{E}$ is a trivial vector bundle on $\mathbb{P}^{\dim X}$.

Question: Does there exist a normal projective variety $X$ (with some choice of very ample embedding) that admits no Ulrich sheaf?
artifact.status_search_result: The existence of Ulrich sheaves on (normal) projective varieties is widely cited as still open. Recent works (e.g., 2025 preprints on existence of Ulrich sheaves and on Ulrich bundles on projective bundles) continue to investigate the problem in special cases, and the general existence question—including the normal case—remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Some evidence for the existence of Ulrich bundles
status_evidence.snippet: The case of Ulrich sheaves has been object of deep study in the last two decades and the problem of their existence is still wide open.
status_evidence.claim: The existence problem for Ulrich sheaves on projective varieties remains open.

status_evidence.title: On existence of Ulrich sheaf
status_evidence.snippet: Mukherjee–Barik, 2025 preprint investigating conditions for existence of Ulrich sheaves on various varieties.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2025) work still investigates existence rather than providing a complete resolution.
